Solution 1's inequality is the wrong one. Log-convexity at $n$ requires $Q_n \ge 1$, not $Q_4 \le Q_3$. Its $M_n$ and $Q_3$, $Q_4$ computations are correct, but $Q_3 \ge 1$ gives $9x \ge 8(x+1)$, i.e. $x \ge 8$. Its claimed threshold $c \approx 19.28$ is also contradicted directly: at $x=10$, $Q_3 \approx 1.023$, $Q_4 > 1$, $Q_5 \approx 1.030$, and $Q_6 \approx 1.031$, so log-convexity holds for $n \le 6$ where the solution predicts failure.

Solution 2 ($c=-1/2$) gives no real justification. Solution 3 ($c=1$) is contradicted by the same $Q_3$ computation: at $x=5$, $M_2M_4 = 1500 < 1600 = M_3^2$, so log-convexity fails there.

The true threshold appears to be at least 8, but I have not fully established the exact value of $c$. None of the three proposed values matches the constraints I could check.

CHOICE: NONE
